ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of directors, shareholders, UBOs, and related counsel against PEP databases, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Luxembourg FIU notices. Enhanced due diligence required for any PEP, beneficial owner resident in a high-risk jurisdiction, or entity subject to targeted financial sanctions. Screening must be completed before incorporation and re-run at least every 90 calendar days or upon any material change in ownership or management.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Latin alphabetic characters. The name must end with the legal form suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL' in French, or 'Gesellschaft mit beschränkter Haftung' in German. The name must be distinctive and not misleading. Non-Latin script names must be rendered into an approved Latin-script transliteration acceptable to the RCS. The registered version is the language in which the deed is drawn, whether French or German.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a name reservation, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request via the LBR platform addressed to the Registrar within 15 days of the rejection. If the registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may submit an administrative appeal before the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) of Luxembourg within three months of the notification. Legal grounds include violation of procedural rules, factual error, or disproportionate refusal. A further appeal lies to the Administrative Court (Cour administrative).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for this service sector. ISIC 6910 commercial litigation chambers and licensed legal activities require a physical registered office in Luxembourg with actual business premises where client files, trust accounts, and management records can be retained and where meetings of management may be held. A mailing address or virtual office does not meet the substance requirements of Luxembourg law and the Code of Civil Procedure for service of process.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% annual probability of unannounced on-site inspections by the competent supervisory authorities, given the statutory licence and AML/CFT obligations imposed on legal service providers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales (Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, consolidated, as amended by the Law of 23 June 2016 modernizing the SARL), Articles 710-1 to 710-24 governing SARL formation, minimum capital, shares, management and governance; supplemented by the Loi du 10 août 1991 sur la profession d'avocat (Law of 10 August 1991 on the legal profession) and the Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 (AML/CFT obligations for law firms).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) as the statutory national business registry under the Ministry of Justice; electronic filing via the LBR e-file portal (lbr.lu).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte de constitution / Statuts (Articles of Incorporation) executed as a notarial deed (acte notarié) or private deed (acte sous seing privé), filed at the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital EUR 12,000 (≈ USD 13,080), fully subscribed and fully paid up in cash at incorporation; cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked escrow account in the name of the 'SARL en formation' with a Luxembourg credit institution (or an EU/EEA credit institution under Article 710-6 of the Law of 1915); the bank issues a blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) that is released only upon presentation of the RCS registration extract; in-kind contributions require a statutory auditor's report and immediate full delivery.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for value added tax; unified electronic access via MyGuichet.lu and the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign parent establishing a Luxembourg SARL, the company is first registered with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) through the Luxembourg Business Registers portal, which automatically issues the national business registration number (matricule). Following incorporation, the SARL must file the AEDT VAT registration request (formulaire 640) via MyGuichet.lu, obtaining a Luxembourg VAT identification number (numéro de TVA); the application is processed within 5–10 business days. A foreign non-resident entity with no Luxembourg fixed establishment that performs taxable domestic supplies must appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative (représentant responsable solidaire) and register immediately, with no turnover threshold; the engagement of legal counsel in Luxembourg is typically undertaken directly by the SARL, which registers for VAT in its own name.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Luxembourg SARL is a resident corporate entity subject to full Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax; it is not eligible for pass-through/check-the-box treatment. The SARL is taxed on its worldwide income unless relief applies via treaty or the territorial provisions for foreign permanent establishments; legal services rendered abroad are not automatically territorial and require a foreign PE analysis under applicable double tax treaties.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections: (i) group taxation regime (intégration fiscale) under Article 164bis LIR for direct or indirect 95% ownership held for at least 24 months, covering corporate income tax and municipal business tax; (ii) the participation exemption (Article 166 LIR) for qualifying dividends and capital gains; (iii) the optional transfer-pricing documentation summary (CbC local file elections). Luxembourg has no check-the-box regime; hybrid mismatch rules (ATAD) restrict deduction/non-inclusion outcomes for hybrid instruments, hybrid entities, and reverse hybrid structures, which are relevant for cross-border litigation fee payments and IP cost-sharing arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Zero for non-resident taxable persons — any foreign supply of services or goods subject to Luxembourg VAT triggers immediate registration or reverse-charge compliance; the domestic small-business exemption of EUR 35,000 annual turnover applies solely to Luxembourg-established taxable persons and does not shelter a foreign SARL branch or a foreign law firm. For cross-border commercial litigation services supplied to a taxable business customer established abroad, the place of supply is the customer's jurisdiction and no Luxembourg VAT registration is required for that specific supply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No universal B2B e-invoicing clearance mandate is currently in force; mandatory B2G (public procurement) e-invoicing via the PEPPOL network applies, phased in under Luxembourg law. VAT-registered businesses must file periodic recapitulative statements (VIES) for intra-Community services and goods, transmit Intrastat declarations where applicable, and retain invoices in a structured audit-valid format (PDF/A-3 or XML/UBL). Luxembourg is transposing the EU ViDA framework, which will introduce real-time digital reporting and e-invoicing clearance for B2B supplies in the near term; cross-border litigation service providers should prepare for transactional digital stamping and API-based reporting.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% VAT) applies to (i) intra-Community supplies of goods to a VAT-identified customer, (ii) exports of goods outside the EU, and (iii) cross-border B2B services, including commercial litigation, arbitration, and legal representation, where the place of supply is in the customer's jurisdiction (Articles 14 and 16 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, consistent with EU place-of-supply rules). The SARL rendering litigation services to a foreign taxable client must not charge Luxembourg VAT provided the client's VAT identification number, business status, and country of establishment are documented; for B2C clients established abroad, legal services are generally taxable in Luxembourg unless an exception applies, hence contract-level factual substantiation is critical.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD / Document Administratif Unique) or equivalent Intrastat/EXS declaration for goods; for services, a recapitulative statement is required where intra-Community B2B services exceed the relevant filing thresholds.
Bill of Lading / CMR waybill / Air Waybill evidencing physical movement of goods out of the EU, where the litigation engagement involves physical exhibits, assets, or goods.

Commercial invoice and engagement letter for the legal services, clearly identifying the client, the nature of the cross-border litigation, the VAT status of the client, and the place of establishment.

Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank SWIFT payment proof demonstrating receipt of foreign consideration, used to substantiate the genuine cross-border nature of the transaction and support transfer-pricing and VAT zero-rating positions.
VIES extraction and a statement of the client's valid VAT identification number in the case of intra-Community B2B services.
Power of attorney and court/arbitral tribunal appointment documents linking the service to the foreign jurisdiction.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.note_on_fx_deadline: Luxembourg law imposes no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark represents the standard internal compliance window applied by Luxembourg practitioners for payment collection, VAT documentary retention, and the AEDT's export substantiation expectations. In practice, the general VAT audit limitation is 5 years (10 years for fraud), and legal fees should be settled and remitted within normal commercial terms to avoid reclassification as a deemed Luxembourg supply.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and Luxembourg Customs scrutinize zero-rating claims through cross-border data exchanges and risk-based audits. Failure to substantiate the export or cross-border place-of-supply within the required documentation triggers a retrospective VAT assessment at the standard rate of 17% (or reduced rates where applicable), disallowance of input-VAT credits, and recapture of any refund already granted. Late payment interest accrues at the statutory rate, and deliberate fraud or the use of false documentation to claim zero-rating attracts administrative fines of up to EUR 25,000 per infringement, penalties of 50%–200% of the evaded tax, and criminal liability under the Luxembourg General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung), including imprisonment for aggravated tax fraud; the clawback period extends to 10 years in cases of fraudulent concealment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in cooperation with the European Central Bank (ECB); banking and financial-market supervision is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility. Luxembourg is a Eurozone OECD member with unrestricted current-account and capital-account flows under Article 63 TFEU and Directive 88/361/EEC. No exchange-control permit or central-bank investment authorization exists for a SARL. Profit remittance hurdles are fiscal rather than currency-related: distributions incur the 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax unless reduced by treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption, and the SARL remains subject to standard corporate income tax and municipal business tax. Foreign-currency accounts may be held and converted freely; exchange spreads and transfer costs are the only practical constraints.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender obligation, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation timeline applies to export proceeds or service income, including cross-border legal fees. The BCL only imposes statistical balance-of-payments reporting for cross-border flows exceeding published thresholds; legal-services revenue and intra-EU group flows fall under the monthly BCL reporting framework but are subject to no currency conversion mandate.

Operational Account and dedicated Escrow/Trust Account
Operational Account; wealth-grade documentation suited to multi-jurisdictional fee flows
Operational Account and Professional Client Funds Deposit Account
Operational Account and correspondent-clearing cash management

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium: feasible and legally permissible for the SARL's own treasury balances, FX conversion and daily operating disbursements through Luxembourg-licensed electronic money institutions or EU-passported EMIs; however, EMIs are NOT viable for client money or litigation settlement funds because Luxembourg fiduciary and escrow rules require client funds to be held with a credit institution in a segregated account. Recommended architecture: an EMI as a liquidity and expense side-rail, with Tier-1 bank accounts as the exclusive clearing and client-funds spine.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory blanket requirement for physical board appearance under the Luxembourg AML/CTF law (Law of 12 November 2004 as amended) and CSSF Regulation 12-02. Remote onboarding is acceptable where high-grade video-KYC, auditable electronic identification, and apostilled corporate documentation satisfy the bank's due-diligence policy. In practice, Luxembourg Tier-1 banks typically require at least one physical or notarized director interview, or a proxy appearance by a Luxembourg-resident domiciliation agent holding a certified power of attorney, before activating dual-purpose client-money accounts; fully remote opening is realistic only for a plain operational account, while litigation client-funds accounts almost always trigger enhanced due diligence meetings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commingling of client settlement monies with operating capital in one treasury account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed client money segregation policy; dedicated séquestre ledger reconciliation; tripartite escrow agreements; professional indemnity insurance certificate; CSSF-compliant audit trail demonstrating transactional separation

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound high-value wires originating from foreign court registries, arbitral tribunals, or settlement escrow agents in moderate-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Engagement and retainer letter; final or interim arbitral/court award; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declarations; chain-of-title on receivables; full EU/OFAC/UN sanctions screening logs with cleared-result evidence

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque or multi-layer beneficial ownership above the SARL, such as non-EU holding shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs extract; signed beneficial-owner declaration per CSSF Regulation 12-02 forms; full organizational chart; notarial deeds; certified passport copies of all natural persons holding directly or indirectly 25% or more of capital or voting rights

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High volume of disbursement payments to third parties such as foreign counsel, expert witnesses, court interpreters, and investigative agencies with vague payment references
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Itemized case-cost memoranda; counterparty invoices and contracts; reverse customer due diligence files on each recipient; standardized fee-billing schedules; privileged legal work-product logs; written client pre-approvals for each cost category

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected inbound transfers during litigation peaks causing unexplained turnover versus projected activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cash-flow forecasting models reconcilable to live dockets; monthly trust-ledger certification by statutory auditor; engagement backlog summary; historical settlement patterns demonstrating the episodic but legitimate nature of litigation receipts

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections, whether share-capital subscription or shareholder loans, must arrive by SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR legs with unambiguous beneficiary naming and a clear remittance purpose. For equity subscription, use the BCL balance-of-payments direct-investment category E (equity capital) and annotate the notarial deed and RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) filing reference in SWIFT field 70; for shareholder loans, use the intercompany financial-loan category referencing the dated loan agreement and shareholders' resolution. The receiving bank will require the notarized subscription deed, an RCS excerpt not older than three months, and board minutes authorizing the facility. EUR legs settle across TARGET2; USD and GBP legs clear via nostro and correspondent networks.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for all non-SEPA cross-border disbursements including foreign counsel fees, court and arbitration costs, expert-witness charges, and asset-tracing vendor payments; SEPA Credit Transfer (pain.001) covers EUR payments inside the SEPA zone with next-day value; Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600 are permissible where litigation security bonds or collateralized settlements require documentary collection mechanics; securities-linked collateral operations use Clearstream Banking Luxembourg and TARGET2-Securities interoperability. Standard practice: instruct wires with detailed purpose codes, such as the BCL balance-of-payments code for legal and other professional services, and pre-agree beneficiary KYC documentation to avoid clearing delays.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX forwards in EUR/USD, EUR/GBP and EUR/CHF under ISDA 2002 or a local Luxembourg master agreement, permitted without BCL authorization
FX swaps for treasury liquidity conversion between EUR, USD and GBP, permitted under CSSF MiFID II rules where the SARL qualifies as an eligible professional counterparty
Non-deliverable forwards in non-convertible or restricted currencies solely to hedge litigation and settlement exposures in jurisdictions where physical currency delivery is legally impeded

Purchased premium-bearing vanilla FX options to hedge fee income and settlement receivables, permitted; writing naked options is not recommended and may constitute dealing activity requiring CSSF licensing

Cross-currency interest rate swaps applicable to term-structured litigation funding receivables, permitted under EU EMIR with clearing obligation and trade-reporting assessment, typically only where notional exposure exceeds EUR 10 million

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of approved annual accounts (financial statements) with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' approval within six months of financial year-end and RCS deposit within one month of approval; for a calendar-year SARL, annual accounts must be filed no later than 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit triggers an RCS formal reminder; the commercial court may impose coercive fines and order compliance; continued default exposes the SARL to court-ordered strike-off and the directors to civil and criminal sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial-owner information in the Luxembourg RBE register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the anniversary of the entity's RBE registration; any change in beneficial ownership must be updated within one month of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors and officers face administrative fines, criminal penalties, and entity-level sanctions; inaccurate or absent annual confirmation creates adverse regulatory flags and undermines reliance on the register for AML/KYC purposes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined annual corporate income tax return covering corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year SARL, the filing deadline is 31 December of the following year; extensions may be granted on written request through the ACD electronic filing portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Every commenced month of delay triggers late-filing penalties and late-payment interest; unpaid amounts are enforced by tax distraint proceedings, and persistent non-compliance may result in enforcement against bank accounts and company assets.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit applies when the SARL exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at two consecutive balance sheet dates: total assets EUR 4.4 million, annual net turnover EUR 8.8 million, or an average workforce of 50 employees. Mandatory audit also applies to credit institutions, insurance and reinsurance undertakings, securitisation vehicles, regulated AIF/AIFM structures, and other supervised public-interest entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 and the Commercial Code accounting provisions; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted or required for consolidated accounts and listed entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must file and annually confirm all beneficial ownership particulars in the RBE within one month of the annual RBE registration anniversary. Any transfer of shares, change in control, or change in beneficial ownership must be reported with updated identity documentation within one month after becoming known to the company.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 – USD 3,800 per annum for registered office and resident professional agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – USD 25,000 for a Luxembourg GAAP statutory audit when mandatory

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% corporate income tax (IRC) plus 7% employment fund surcharge plus municipal business tax (Luxembourg City headline 6.75%), producing a combined headline rate of 24.94% on taxable income; first EUR 175,000 of taxable income is taxed at 15% IRC.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains; 80% exemption on qualifying intellectual property income; investment tax credit of 7%-9%; R&D super-deduction; notional interest deduction on qualifying equity; flat 15% IRC bracket under EUR 175,000; no withholding tax on ordinary cross-border interest and royalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu with LuxTrust authentication; paper filings accepted under limited ex officio conditions.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File by 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end; extension of up to six months may be requested before the statutory deadline where supported by Belgian/Luxembourg bookkeeping closure conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification: RCSL registration number, legal form (SARL), registered office, trade scope under ISIC 6910.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Luxembourg permanent establishment (PE) registration details and the foreign parent RCS number; ensure the PE is clearly designated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net turnover and gross receipts from cross-border commercial litigation, arbitration, and asset tracing services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare only revenue economically attributable to the Luxembourg PE; do not include fees recorded in foreign chambers or under foreign professional contracts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: salaries of local counsel, expert witness fees, rent, court disbursements, insurance, and administrative overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses actually incurred for the Luxembourg PE; intercompany allocations must comply with the arm's-length standard and be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses: fines, tax penalties, non-eligible gifts, excessive representation costs, and expenses connected to exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List PE-specific non-deductible charges; a non-resident must exclude overhead allocated abroad that is not attributable to Luxembourg source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income and participation exemption deductions: qualifying dividends, liquidation surpluses, and capital gains on 10%-plus qualifying shareholdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply participation exemption only if the PE holds the qualifying shares and the 12-month holding period and anti-abuse substance conditions are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward utilisation under Article 110 LIR: available losses within the 17-year window.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only losses of the Luxembourg PE; a change of more than 50% in ownership may restrict utilisation under the anti-abuse rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adjustments and offsets; the base for applying the 17% IRC and the 15% bracket.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute Luxembourg-source PE income only; a nil or negative balance is acceptable where supported by the loss schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, advance CIT payments, and foreign tax credits attributable to Luxembourg-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credits only for taxes borne directly by the Luxembourg PE on the same income stream; do not credit residence-state taxes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an administrative fine of EUR 50 to EUR 1,000 per return; a 10% tax surcharge applies when a return is filed after the due date and tax remains payable; late payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month or fraction thereof (7.2% per annum); deliberate omission or falsification constitutes tax fraud with fines up to EUR 150,000 and imprisonment up to five years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic dividend withholding tax; reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for a qualifying parent holding at least 10% for at least 12 months; treaty rates typically range from 0% to 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must provide the Luxembourg paying agent with a current Tax Residence Certificate issued by the treaty state, a beneficial ownership declaration, and proof of the shareholding period. Withholding at the reduced treaty rate can be applied at source only after the recipient supplies these documents to the Luxembourg withholding agent; otherwise the 15% statutory withholding is made and the excess is recoverable via a refund claim before the Luxembourg direct tax administration (Administration des contributions directes), generally within the statutory limitation period of three years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rate is 0% withholding tax on ordinary arm's-length interest and royalties paid to non-residents; a 15% withholding tax applies to profit-participating loans or interest economically equivalent to dividends. Under tax treaties, interest and royalty rates are generally reduced to 0%-10%, and the EU Interest and Royalties Directive (2003/49/EC) eliminates withholding tax where a 25% minimum shareholding links the payer and recipient.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 750,000,000 group consolidated revenue triggers Master File and Country-by-Country Report obligations; Local File is required when annual related-party transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000 for goods or EUR 500,000 for services, based on the Luxembourg transfer pricing administrative guidance; the tax authorities may request documentation at lower thresholds on a case-by-case basis.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no standalone Economic Substances Regulations comparable to OECD low-tax jurisdictions, but economic substance is independently required under the general anti-abuse rule (Section 6 LIR), the ATAD GAAR, the OECD principal purposes test, and Luxembourg administrative circulars on holding and financing companies. A SARL engaged in cross-border litigation services must maintain local premises, qualified and decision-making personnel, and genuine commercial risk in Luxembourg to secure treaty benefits, participation exemption, and reduced dividend withholding treatment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement or concealment of taxable profits, falsification of financial records, or omission of client trust account income derived from cross-border commercial litigation for the purpose of reducing Luxembourg CIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine from EUR 5,000 to EUR 150,000, or an amount up to six times the evaded tax, plus imprisonment ranging from eight days to five years; administrative tax adjustments, 10% late-filing surcharge, and monthly interest of 0.6% on underpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the gérant of the SARL may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate taxes and penalties when the evasion is attributable to deliberate mismanagement; criminal conviction may trigger travel bans, asset freezing, confiscation orders, and civil restitution via the Luxembourg action en comblement du passif.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording artificial intercompany fees, inflated management charges, or conduit invoicing between the Luxembourg SARL and related foreign litigation chambers without economic substance or contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Luxembourg tax administration may re-determine profits under the arm's-length standard, deny deductibility of unsubstantiated charges, impose late-payment interest and negligence penalties, and deny entitlement to tax treaty or EU directive benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for restitution where false or misleading transfer pricing documentation caused a balance-sheet deficit; repeated non-compliance may result in administrative travel bans and disqualification for serious mismanagement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Dividend Repatriation and Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividends through a Luxembourg SARL shell or letterbox entity lacking local substance or business purpose solely to obtain the 0% EU Parent-Subsidiary withholding rate or reduced treaty withholding under an applicable DTA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of the 0% or treaty-reduced rate; retroactive application of the 15% domestic dividend withholding tax; assessment of withholding under-withheld penalties and monthly interest; possible determination of the Luxembourg entity as a fully taxable shell with sanctions under the GAAR.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible director is personally liable for any withholding tax the company failed to account for, plus related fines; in fraud circumstances, the director may face imprisonment and travel bans under mutual assistance in criminal tax matters.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and Shell Company Facade
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SARL to receive and launder litigation proceeds from high-risk jurisdictions, transferring funding without AML/KYC procedures, hiding the ultimate beneficial owner, or maintaining a fraudulent shell structure over the commercial litigation practice.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Luxembourg anti-money laundering law of 12 November 2004 and the 2019/2023 reforms, penalties include imprisonment of one to ten years and fines up to EUR 2,500,000 for natural persons and up to 10% of annual turnover for legal persons; the SARL may be dissolved, client assets confiscated, and beneficiary accounts frozen.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal liability, asset confiscation, travel bans, and director disqualification; they can also be ordered to restore trust funds under civil recovery proceedings where their conduct enabled the laundering of third-party funds.
